Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing assertion in NonLinearConjugateGradientOptimizerTest.testTrivial checks that optimizer.getIterations() > 0 after an optimization run.

What happens in the code:
- BaseOptimizer.optimize parses options and resets the counters:
  - iterations.resetCount() (BaseOptimizer.optimize, lines 139–142).
- BaseOptimizer.getIterations simply returns the internal counter: iterations.getCount() (BaseOptimizer.getIterations, lines 92–94).
- The iteration counter is only incremented when a concrete optimizer calls BaseOptimizer.incrementIterationCount() (lines 171–174).

In NonLinearConjugateGradientOptimizer.doOptimize:
- The method manages its own local iteration variable:
  - int iter = 0; then ++iter at the start of each while-loop cycle (lines 214–218).
- It uses this local iter for the convergence checker (checker.converged(iter, ...), lines 223–226).
- Crucially, it never calls BaseOptimizer.incrementIterationCount() anywhere in the loop.

Effect:
- Because the local iter is incremented but BaseOptimizer’s iteration counter is not, BaseOptimizer.getIterations() remains at 0 throughout the optimization.
- Consequently, the test’s assertion optimizer.getIterations() > 0 fails.

Relation to the current bug report:
- The report notes that getIterations() always returns 0 (observed for another optimizer, LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer). This is the same class of problem: concrete optimizers must call BaseOptimizer.incrementIterationCount() during their iteration loops. NonLinearConjugateGradientOptimizer exhibits exactly this issue, leading to the failed test here.

Root cause:
- Missing calls to BaseOptimizer.incrementIterationCount() in NonLinearConjugateGradientOptimizer.doOptimize; the method uses a private counter instead of updating the shared BaseOptimizer iteration counter that getIterations() reports.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
